proposals.title: What a Groth16 setup is tied to
proposals.bookReference: B08-EXACT-MANUSCRIPT-SECTIONS.json: source B07-proving-nothing.md lines 272-298 (seven-layer overview) and 609-621 (Universal versus Circuit-Specific Setups); B05, same heading.
proposals.sourceSupport: G02 (snarkjs README and guide) uses compiled circuits and describes common Phase 1 plus circuit-specific Phase 2. G04 (Filecoin Phase2 Attestations README) says Phase 2 is per circuit. G05 (Groth 2016 paper abstract) supports proof shape, not a Webs circuit inventory.
proposals.websiteMapping: Make Layer 1 a visible technical section. Explain setup parameters and keys in plain language, then make circuit-specific versus shared setup material explicit. Distinguish circuit structure from statement and witness values.
proposals.readerCopy: Groth16 setup is tied to a compiled circuit. Reusing that circuit for different inputs does not by itself require a new setup. Change its constraints or supported bounds, and you may have a different circuit that needs its own Phase 2 setup.
proposals.interaction: Expandable two-column explainer: 'same circuit, new inputs' versus 'changed compiled constraints'; show whether the example changes the circuit-specific setup count, with a note that the compiled artifact determines the answer.
proposals.diagram: Circuit source and compiler -> compiled circuit C1 -> Phase 2 setup and keys for C1. Two different statement/witness instances enter the same C1 box and share its circuit identity. A changed compiled circuit C2 branches to its own Phase 2 setup.
questions: Which compilation artifact and compatibility criteria will the site treat as identifying a distinct circuit?
Does the supported toolchain expose a reliable circuit digest for readers to inspect?
proposals.limits: Do not imply input-value changes trigger setup. Do not present source-code equality alone as proof of compiled-circuit identity. Final cryptographic wording belongs to Opus 5.5.

proposals.title: One shared Phase 1 can feed many Phase 2 setups
proposals.bookReference: B05, 'Universal versus Circuit-Specific Setups'; B08 source lines 609-621. The book’s contrast is between circuit-specific Groth16 setup and universal-SRS proof systems.
proposals.sourceSupport: G02 says projects can pick a round from common Phase 1 for circuit-specific Phase 2. G04 says Filecoin ran Phase 1 once and uses its output for each circuit’s Phase 2. These support the phase distinction for the cited workflows, not universal compatibility across arbitrary curves or parameter sizes.
proposals.websiteMapping: Show ceremony counts by phase rather than a single unlabeled 'setup count'. Allow a compatible shared Phase 1 row and a per-distinct-circuit Phase 2 row, with compatibility assumptions visible.
proposals.readerCopy: A compatible Phase 1 transcript can be shared. Groth16 still needs a circuit-specific Phase 2 setup for each distinct compiled circuit. Sharing Phase 1 does not turn Groth16 into a universal per-circuit key system.
proposals.interaction: For a hypothetical K, show K Phase 2 setups and one shared Phase 1 only when the selected circuits fit the same Phase 1 domain. Let the reader toggle separate Phase 1 domains to see the count change.
proposals.diagram: Compatible Phase 1 transcript -> parallel branches to Circuit A / Phase 2 A, Circuit B / Phase 2 B, ... Circuit K / Phase 2 K. Caption: 'Illustrative; K is user supplied; compatibility must be established.'
questions: What curve, size bound, and setup implementation would define a compatible Phase 1 domain for the intended example?
Should page terminology count phases, ceremonies, or ceremony rounds separately?
proposals.limits: The K calculator is hypothetical only. Do not claim one Phase 1 covers all Cardano circuits or combine incompatible setup domains.

proposals.title: Why the Cardano-wide setup total is unknown
proposals.bookReference: B08 source lines 272-298 and 609-621; the chapter presents setup as one layer of a broader, interdependent system.
proposals.sourceSupport: V2-COPY.json says the 235 identifiers are pre-dedup review identifiers, not proven properties, and labels retained families as requirements rather than supported ports; it explicitly says required setup count is unknown. G04 illustrates that a circuit inventory must account for variants: its note distinguishes 32GiB and 64GiB phase2 setups.
proposals.websiteMapping: Place a short inventory status beside the calculator. Explain that a count needs a defined scope, a compiled-circuit inventory, versions/variants, and setup-domain compatibility. Keep Cardano ecosystem scope separate from the Webs catalogue.
proposals.readerCopy: We cannot give a reliable setup total for all Cardano applications from this catalogue. The 235 review identifiers and 20 families are not compiled-circuit counts. The total remains unknown until the scope and circuit inventory are established.
proposals.interaction: A transparent inventory worksheet can accept named circuits and variants as hypothetical entries, then calculate Phase 2 counts and shared Phase 1 domains. Default to an empty inventory and show 'No audited total available.'
proposals.diagram: Scope definition -> deduplicated compiled-circuit inventory -> group by compatible Phase 1 domain -> count one Phase 2 per distinct circuit; display unknown until the inventory is sourced.
questions: What exact boundary does 'entire Cardano' mean: deployed applications at a date, one protocol family, or future application possibilities?
Which deployed circuits, versions, parameter variants, curves, and ceremony records can be sourced and verified?
How will identical circuits reused by multiple applications be deduplicated?
proposals.limits: Do not infer a total from review IDs, project families, applications, or transaction instances. Do not claim the website has surveyed Cardano’s deployed circuits.

proposals.title: Bundling cases can change the count, within explicit bounds
proposals.bookReference: B08 source lines 272-298 on layer interdependence and lines 609-621 on circuit-specific setup and alternatives.
proposals.sourceSupport: G02 and G04 support that Phase 2 is tied to a circuit in their Groth16 workflows. The supplied materials do not demonstrate a Moriarty generic circuit or prove that bundling would be efficient or safe.
proposals.websiteMapping: Offer parameterized and bundled relations as design options in a clearly hypothetical panel. Describe the tradeoff between fewer compiled circuits and a broader/larger relation; require explicit limits and do not claim future-proof coverage.
proposals.readerCopy: A single circuit can sometimes express several bounded cases, which may reduce the number of circuit-specific setups. It covers only the cases and limits encoded in that circuit. New cases outside those limits still need a changed circuit and setup.
proposals.interaction: Compare K separate hypothetical circuits with one hypothetical bounded bundle. Show the assumed relation coverage and mark circuit size, performance, auditability, and setup suitability as unknown until measured and reviewed.
proposals.diagram: Option A: Relation 1 -> Circuit 1 / Phase 2; Relation 2 -> Circuit 2 / Phase 2. Option B: bounded Relation 1+2 -> Circuit B / Phase 2, with the bound and selector logic drawn inside the circuit box.
questions: Can the intended relation safely encode the cases behind this proposed bundle, including selector and range checks?
What resource, review, and maintenance costs would bundling add?
Would a bound change alter the compiled constraints and require a new Phase 2 setup?
proposals.limits: Present as a design possibility, not an existing Webs capability or a solution for all future Cardano programs. No universal bounded circuit can be assumed to cover unspecified future relations.
